name: True Faith, Holy Ground and Relics (Dark Ages)

pages.name: True Faith, Holy Ground and Relics (Dark Ages)

text.content:
In the Dark Medieval, the Church is both spiritual and temporal power, and True Faith is a palpable threat to every Cainite. True Faith is not limited to Christianity — Jews, Muslims, pagans, and heretics can hold it as strongly (or more strongly) than any Christian, since the strength of conviction matters more than the truth of the belief. Only mortals may possess True Faith; the Embrace strips a vampire of the purity it requires, though a devoutly faithful Cainite on the Road of Heaven may occasionally touch its edges.

Repelling Vampires

A character with True Faith may brandish a holy symbol and call a Social Challenge to repel a vampire. Success forces the vampire to test for Rötschreck or flee immediately; failure still forces the vampire back a few feet to cower, unable to attack next turn (though she may still defend herself). A vampire may resist only by overbidding with Willpower — if she has at least twice the Willpower Traits of the faithful character, she is unaffected. Multiple vampires can be repelled with a group challenge. Any time a test involving True Faith fails, the faithful character suffers a crisis of faith: one Trait down on all Social Challenges for the rest of the scene, unable to invoke Faith again until it is restored at the Narrator's discretion.

Holy Symbols and Blessed Items

Brandishing a holy symbol grants the Social Trait Daunting when repelling the undead or warding off supernatural powers. Striking a supernatural creature with it grants the Physical Traits Burning and Searing and inflicts one level of aggravated damage. Any of the faithful can bless an item over a half-hour religious ceremony (one blessing per session per character, one blessing per item at a time), granting it a Bonus Trait (Burning, Searing, Blinding, Branding, Purging, Cleansing, or Purifying) usable in a Physical Challenge against a supernatural creature. If that challenge is lost, the Trait and the blessing are both gone; if won, the item causes one level of aggravated damage instead of its normal damage. Holy water causes one level of aggravated damage per splash, or per turn of immersion, without gaining Bonus Traits. A devout, non-Faith-rated priest can still bless holy water, wine, and communion wafers.

Relics

Relics are rare items imbued with centuries of collective faith and require Storyteller approval to introduce; even false relics (fake bones, forged fragments) can develop their own Faith rating over time if venerated sincerely enough. A relic's touch inflicts aggravated damage on a supernatural creature (Storyteller sets the level, four being a practical maximum) and forces a Courage Test against that damage to avoid fleeing. Additional relic powers should reflect whatever the item or saint was known for.

Gifts of Faith

A character's Faith rating can be added to the difficulty of Static Challenges made to influence her mind, heart or soul (Dominate, Presence, etc.), or treated as Traits up in the challenge, and it can be added to her Conscience rating for Conscience Challenges. Cainites feeding on someone with True Faith must drink additional Blood Traits equal to her Faith rating just to gain a single Blood Trait; blood from someone with Faith x3 or greater is actively harmful, inflicting a level of aggravated damage per Trait drunk with no benefit gained.

With the right trappings (salt, crucifixes, holy water) the faithful can perform the following, using a Static Social Challenge (adding Faith rating) against the listed difficulty. Without the trappings, the character is one Trait down.

TaskDifficulty
Force a ghost to fleeGhost's Willpower
Permanently expel a ghostGhost's Willpower + 2
Force a minor demon to fleeSix Traits
Force a major demon to fleeEight Traits
Permanently expel a demon10 Traits
Ward against Dominate/PresenceSix Traits (adds Faith rating to the challenge)
Banish effects of Dominate/PresenceVampire's Willpower
Sever a blood oath10 Traits
Inflict (Faith rating) levels of aggravated damage on a demon, ghost, or vampireEight Traits

The faithful may also heal by touch, granting health levels for healing-time and difficulty purposes only (e.g., a Wounded patient blessed by a priest with Faith x3 is treated as Bruised for recovery purposes) until the patient next attempts to heal naturally; this cannot raise the dead but can save the dying and cures illness or poison as readily as injury. Some of the faithful can also sense a nearby vampire, ghost, or demon with a successful Mental Challenge (unaffected by Obfuscate, Obtenebration, Stealth, or other concealment) whenever they are at peace — praying, meditating, even sleeping — but not while distracted or occupied.

Holy Ground

Churches, mosques, shrines, and monasteries with strong faithful resonance make supernatural creatures wary. A vampire must win a Courage check (difficulty set by the Storyteller based on the ground's holiness) to enter such a place, and remains one Trait down on all challenges while inside. All blood expenditure doubles on holy ground, and perception-affecting Disciplines (Auspex, Chimerstry) suffer a two-Trait penalty. Characters with True Faith gain a Bonus Trait on any challenge made on holy ground consecrated to their own beliefs.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Five: Rules, Systems and Drama
